vehicles.name: BUS 13,7 - 13,7 m bus

source.title: Grundlag for udformning af trafikarealer
source.figure: Type vehicle diagram, PDF page 39; steering table Figure 6.7, PDF page 49
source.notes: Dimension chain 2,61 + 6,45 + 1,49 + 3,15 = 13,7 m. The rearmost axle is a medløbsaksel -- a self-steering trailing axle, which the published curves assume -- so it carries no side force and the drive axle is the effective rear-axle reference; the 1,49 m to the trailing axle is therefore folded into the 4,64 m rear overhang. Body width excludes mirrors. Mode A uses 33 gon, represented as 29.7 degrees; mode B uses the published 46 gon converted exactly, 41.4 degrees, rather than the 41 the same table prints beside it. Axle track and tyre width are measured from the published plan-view figure at its own scale.

vehicles.validationNotes: Dimensions are source-transcribed. BUS 13,7 is absent from certification-plan.json because no official DWG for it was collected, but it is corroborated against the legacy Vejdirektoratet curve library, which also confirms the effective rear-axle choice the medløbsaksel forces -- see LegacyCurveAgreementTests.

vehicles.name: PVT - Påhængsvogntog

source.title: Grundlag for udformning af trafikarealer
source.figure: Type vehicle diagram, PDF page 42; steering table Figure 6.7, PDF page 49
source.notes: Dimension chains 1,4 + 5,5 + 2,15 for the lorry and 1,2 + 5,8 + 1,15 for the trailer, 18,75 m overall. The drawbar is drawn from a coupling dimensioned 0,15 m inside the lorry's rear face -- 2,00 m behind its rear axle -- to the trailer's front axle, 2,90 m further back. That front axle is the turntable the trailer body pivots on, so the combination is modelled as two joints, not one: drawbar about the coupling, body about the turntable. Body width excludes mirrors. Mode A uses 33 gon, represented as 29.7 degrees; mode B uses the published 43 gon converted exactly, 38.7 degrees, rather than the 38 the same table prints alongside it; the official PVT curve sheet holds an outer radius implying 38.9 degrees, which is what settled the choice for both combinations. Axle track and tyre width are measured from the published plan-view figure at its own scale, not from a DWG vehicle block as PV, REN and BUS 12 are, and carry about 0.01 m of measurement uncertainty.

vehicles.validationNotes: Dimensions are source-transcribed. The official-DWG certification matrix reconstructs a rigid body from paired wheel traces and has no articulated case, so PVT is absent from certification-plan.json rather than failing in it. It is partly corroborated instead against the legacy Vejdirektoratet curve library: on the mode-B sheets at 140, 160 and 180 gon the lorry holds a sustained full-lock arc whose outer radius matches this preset to 0.036 m, which measures its wheelbase, front overhang, width and wheel angle together. The trailer is not corroborated -- the combination is still folding at 180 gon, the longest turn the library draws, so no sheet shows it in a steady turn. Unlike SVT, every body edge is dimensioned in the published plan view, so no overhang here is assumed. The drawbar carries no body of its own and sweeps nothing.

vehicles.name: SVT - Sættevogntog

source.title: Grundlag for udformning af trafikarealer
source.figure: Type vehicle diagram, PDF page 43; steering table Figure 6.7, PDF page 49
source.notes: Dimension chain 1,4 + 3,6 + 8,3 + 3,2 = 16,5 m, with the kingpin dimensioned 0,6 m ahead of the tractor drive axle; the semitrailer wheelbase is therefore 0,6 + 8,3 = 8,9 m from kingpin to trailer axle. The trailer box front sits 3,2 m behind the bumper in the side view, which is 10,1 m ahead of the trailer axle. Body width excludes mirrors. Mode A uses 33 gon, represented as 29.7 degrees; mode B uses the published 43 gon converted exactly, 38.7 degrees, rather than the 38 the same table prints alongside it -- the official PVT curve sheet is drawn to an outer radius implying 38.9 degrees, so the exact conversion is the one the curves were made with and the rounded figure is 0.17 m out. Axle track and tyre width are measured from the published plan-view figure at its own scale, not from a DWG vehicle block as PV, REN and BUS 12 are, and carry about 0.01 m of measurement uncertainty; the same method reproduces the DWG-measured PV axle track to 0.001 m.

vehicles.validationNotes: Dimensions are source-transcribed and not corroborated against any drawn reference. The official-DWG certification matrix reconstructs a rigid body from paired wheel traces and has no articulated case, so SVT is absent from certification-plan.json rather than failing in it; and the legacy curve library cannot corroborate it either, because a semitrailer on this tractor has no steady turn at any lock either mode allows, so no sheet holds an arc to measure. Its two tightest mode-B sheets are also structurally broken. Two figures are assumptions rather than transcriptions, because the published plan view draws the combination as one 16,5 m envelope and dimensions no split between tractor and trailer: the tractor rear overhang (1,00 m behind the drive axle) and, with it, where the tractor body ends under the trailer. Both sit inside the trailer footprint when the combination is straight and affect only the inside of a hard fold.

vehicles.name: SK - Specialkøretøj (22 m, fast bagaksel)

source.title: Grundlag for udformning af trafikarealer
source.figure: Type vehicle diagram, PDF page 44; modes, Figures 6.3 and 6.5 (PDF pages 46-47), PDF page 48 and Figure 6.7 (PDF page 49); official curve sheet reference/vejdirektoratet-koerekurver/02-koeremaade-b/SKT_B.dwg
source.notes: The 22 m variant with a fixed rear axle -- the only one the source dimensions; the 26 m and 30 m variants of PDF page 48 have force-steered axles the model does not represent. Dimension chain 1,2 + 4,8 + 13,4 + 2,6 = 22 m, with the kingpin dimensioned 0,6 m ahead of the tractor's axle reference; the semitrailer wheelbase is therefore 0,6 + 13,4 = 14,0 m, as for SVT (0,6 + 8,3). The chain is drawn to a reference point in each axle group, not to a single axle: the vector copy of the same figure in SKT_B.dwg (block with the same seven dimensions, at true scale in metres) places the tractor's tandem axles 0,614 m either side of the 4,8 m point and the trailer's tri-axle 1,2 m either side of the 13,4 m point, so each reference is its group's centre, the effective-axle convention for fixed axle groups that the official SKT B sheet's own vehicle also uses (kingpin to middle trailer axle 14,0 m, middle axle to tail 2,6 m). The raster figure on PDF page 44 draws both groups ending at those points instead -- same dimensions, axles shifted forward by half the tandem spacing and one tri-axle spacing; the model is unaffected because it carries one effective axle per unit. Not dimensioned in the plan view, so taken from the side view of the same vector figure: the tractor chassis ends 7,705 m behind the bumper, 1,705 m behind its axle reference, and the trailer headboard is 3,96 m behind the bumper, 1,44 m ahead of the kingpin and 15,44 m ahead of the trailer axle (the official SKT B sheet's 18,0 m trailer puts it at 1,40). Body width 2,55 m excludes mirrors; the SKT B sheet's own vehicle is drawn 2,50 m wide. Axle track and tyre width are measured from the vector plan view, as PV and BUS 12 are: every wheel is 0,254 m wide with edges 0,971 m and 1,225 m off the centreline, identical to BUS 12. Mode A uses 33 gon, the general rule of PDF page 48, represented as 29.7 degrees; its speed is 5 km/h, because Figures 6.3 and 6.5 exclude SK from the 15 km/h rows (footnote 1: 'Gælder ikke specialkøretøjer, da der ønskes en lav svinghastighed for disse') and the source publishes no SK mode-A curves at all. Mode B: Figure 6.7 prints '-' for SK with the footnote 'Kørekurver findes for hjuldrejning 11,1/16,7 og 50 gon' and does not say which lock belongs to which variant; 50 gon, 45.0 degrees, is assigned to this 22 m vehicle because the official SKT B sheet, whose vehicle is this one, holds a sustained 8,52 m outer arc at 120 and 140 gon, which a 4,8 m wheelbase and 1,2 m front overhang produce only at that lock (the other two published locks would give about 20 m and 29 m). The 11,1 and 16,7 gon locks are presumed to belong to the force-steered variants and are not offered. lockToLockSeconds 6.0 is a RhinoRoad assumption, as for every preset; the source publishes no steering rate.

vehicles.validationNotes: Dimensions are source-transcribed. The official-DWG certification matrix has no articulated case, so SK is absent from certification-plan.json. The tractor is partly corroborated: the official SKT B sheet (SKT_B.dwg) holds a sustained 8,52 m outer arc about one centre over 4 to 6 m of its 120 and 140 gon envelopes, against 8,52 m predicted for its own 2,50 m-wide vehicle and 8,54 m for this 2,55 m preset at 45.0 degrees. The semitrailer is not corroborated: at 45.0 degrees the tractor's 4,8 m rear-axle radius is far below the 13,99 m a 14,0 m semitrailer on a 0,6 m kingpin needs for a steady state, so no sheet shows it in a steady turn. Two figures are measured rather than dimensioned -- the tractor tail and the trailer nose, see the notes -- and both sit inside the trailer footprint or ahead of the kingpin by under 1,5 m.

vehicles.name: MVT - Modulvogntog

source.title: Grundlag for udformning af trafikarealer
source.figure: Type vehicle diagram, PDF page 43; steering table Figure 6.7, PDF page 49; official curve sheet reference/vejdirektoratet-koerekurver/01-koeremaade-a/Koerekurve_MVT_vifte_11042019_VD.dwg (vehicle 'VEJREGLER 2018 (DK) MVT')
source.notes: The most space-demanding MVT the source names: a three-axle tractor, a link semitrailer whose own two axles carry a second fifth wheel, and a tri-axle semitrailer -- a B-double, three units and two fifth-wheel joints. The figure alone does not settle that: its raster draws the link trailer's axles like a separate dolly, and three of its references sit a few centimetres off one another. The unit split and every articulation point are therefore taken from the vehicle definition in Vejdirektoratet's own MVT curve sheet, which prints the chain 1,42 + 3,19 + 8,48 + 7,78 + 4,31 = 25,18 m (bumper, front axle, tractor fifth wheel, link fifth wheel, semitrailer middle axle, tail) and draws each unit at true scale; the published figure is checked against it link by link. Tractor: 1,42 m front overhang (figure 1,42); its tandem axles sit 2,53 and 3,91 m behind the front axle, so the effective rear axle at the tandem centre is 3,22 m back (figure 3,22 to the same point, with 0,69 m half-spacing); the fifth wheel is 3,19 m behind the front axle, 0,03 m ahead of that centre (the figure dimensions 0,03 but draws it 0,03 behind, a 0,06 m disagreement in the sheet's favour); the tail is the figure's 0,69 + 0,78 = 1,47 m behind the axle reference, because the sheet draws only a narrow chassis there. Link trailer: front 1,60 m ahead of its kingpin, 3,01 m behind the bumper (not dimensioned in the figure, whose side view measures 3,05 m); axles 6,61 and 8,43 m behind the kingpin (figure spacing 1,82), so its effective axle at their centre is 7,52 m from the kingpin; its fifth wheel is 8,48 m behind the kingpin, 0,05 m behind the rear axle (figure 0,05) and so 0,96 m behind the effective axle; its outline runs full width to the tail of the rear tyres, 1,418 m behind the effective axle, because the box ends 6,2 m behind the kingpin (figure 6,21 from the tractor tandem centre) and the tyres fill the 0,78 m between box and semitrailer. Semitrailer: front 1,5 m ahead of its kingpin and middle axle 7,78 m behind it (the figure prints the same 1,5 and 7,78 but draws both from the link's rear axle, 0,05 m ahead of the kingpin), tri-axle spacing 1,31 (figure 1,31), tail 4,31 m behind the middle axle (figure 4,33; 4,31 is what closes the chain on the published 25,18 m). Body width 2,55 m excludes mirrors. Axle track and tyre width are measured from the published plan-view figure at its own scale -- tyre edges about 0,97 and 1,23 m off the centreline -- and taken as SVT's and PVT's 2,195 and 0,254 m, within the method's 0,01 m uncertainty. Mode A uses 33 gon, represented as 29.7 degrees, as every preset does, although the official MVT 15 km/h sheet states a 30.0 degree lock. Mode B uses 38.0 degrees: Figure 6.7 prints 43 gon and 38 degrees, and the official sheet's 5 km/h run states 'STEERING LOCK ANGLE = 38.0 deg.', so here, unlike for SVT and PVT, the rounded figure is the one the curves were drawn with. PDF page 49 says no mode-B curves were drawn for MVT; the 5 km/h run sits in the mode-A folder of the curve download. lockToLockSeconds 6.0 is a RhinoRoad assumption, as for every preset; the source publishes no steering rate.

vehicles.validationNotes: Dimensions are source-transcribed. The official-DWG certification matrix has no articulated case, so MVT is absent from certification-plan.json, and the legacy curve library holds no MVT sheet that can be identified. The tractor is corroborated by the radii the official MVT sheet prints: at 30.0 degrees an 8,28 m front-corner and 6,44 m front-axle radius, at 38.0 degrees 7,12 m and 5,23 m, all of which this preset's 3,22 m wheelbase, 1,42 m front overhang and 2,55 m width reproduce to 0,005 m -- which also confirms the tandem centre as the tractor's effective axle. The sheet's front-wheel radii (7,57 and 6,28 m) put the tyre's outer edge flush with the body, 0,05 m wider than this preset's measured 1,225 m. Neither trailer is corroborated: no steady turn exists at either lock.
